name: Lightning Traps
description: Short, freshly written questions with a tempting fast wrong answer: multi-step unit conversions, fencepost counts, misleading magnitudes, average-speed and percentage traps, calendar arithmetic. The model has 30 seconds per answer (stated in the prompt and enforced by the harness) and must reply with a single FINAL ANSWER line; any extra text scores zero. It measures whether a model stops to think under pressure.
hook: 30 seconds. One line. Don't fall for it.
author: Gauntlet Core
preamble:
LIGHTNING ROUND. Your entire reply must be ONE line, exactly in the form
FINAL ANSWER: <answer>
No working, no explanation, nothing before or after that line: a reply containing anything else scores zero. Give exactly one answer.

cases.prompt: A tap drips once every 2 seconds, and 20 drops make 1 millilitre. How many litres does it drip in one week?
cases.notes: 604,800 s / 2 = 302,400 drops; / 20 = 15,120 ml = 15.12 L. Dividing by 2 or 1000 at the wrong step gives 30.24 or 151.2.

cases.prompt: A straight 1 km road has a lamp post every 25 m, including one at each end. Counting from one end, every 4th post (the 4th, 8th, 12th and so on) is broken. How many posts work?
cases.notes: 1000/25 + 1 = 41 posts; broken: 4, 8, ..., 40 = 10; working 31. Forgetting the extra end post gives 40 - 10 = 30.

cases.prompt: Which is larger: (A) 2 to the power 30, or (B) 10 to the power 9? Answer A or B.
cases.notes: 2^30 = 1,073,741,824 > 1,000,000,000. 'A thousand to the third' intuition says they are about equal and 10^9 is the round-number favourite.

cases.prompt: Which is longer: (A) 1,000,000 seconds, or (B) 11 days and 14 hours? Answer A or B.
cases.notes: 11 days 14 hours = 950,400 + 50,400 = 1,000,800 s, which is 800 s longer than a million seconds.

cases.prompt: A price is raised by 25%, and the new price is then cut by 20%. By how many percent does the final price differ from the original price?
cases.notes: 1.25 x 0.80 = 1.00: no change. Adding percentages gives the lure 5%.

cases.prompt: You drive 60 km at 30 km/h and then another 60 km at 90 km/h. What is your average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?
cases.notes: Total 120 km in 2 h + 40 min = 8/3 h: 45 km/h. The arithmetic mean of the speeds is the lure 60.

cases.prompt: A conference is held on every weekday (Monday to Friday) from Monday 3 June to Friday 14 June, both days included. On how many days is it held?
cases.notes: 3-7 June and 10-14 June: 5 + 5 = 10 (checked against the 2024 calendar, where 3 June is a Monday). 14 - 3 + 1 = 12 ignores the weekend.

cases.prompt: How many times is the digit 7 written when you write out all the whole numbers from 1 to 100?
cases.notes: Units digit: 7, 17, ..., 97 (10); tens digit: 70-79 (10); 77 counts twice: 20. Counted in build.py.

cases.prompt: Tom is twice as old as Ann was when Tom was as old as Ann is now. Tom is 24. How old is Ann?
cases.notes: Let Ann be a; the age gap is 24 - a; when Tom was a, Ann was 2a - 24; 24 = 2(2a - 24) gives a = 18 (brute-forced in build.py). Halving 24 gives the lure 12.

cases.prompt: A car uses 8 litres of fuel per 100 km. How many kilometres can it drive on 50 litres?
cases.notes: 50 / 8 x 100 = 625 km. Multiplying 8 x 50 gives the lure 400.

cases.prompt: At exactly 12:00 the hour and minute hands of a clock are together. How many minutes later are they next exactly together? Give the answer to one decimal place.
cases.notes: The minute hand gains 5.5 degrees per minute; a full 360-degree lap takes 720/11 = 65.45... minutes, 65.5 to one decimal. 'About 1:05' gives the lure 65.

cases.prompt: Which has more mass: one litre of liquid water at 4 °C, or one litre of solid ice? Answer water, ice or same.
cases.notes: Ice (about 0.917 kg per litre) is less dense than water at 4 degrees C (about 1.000 kg per litre), which is why it floats. 'A litre is a litre' gives the lure.

cases.prompt: How many squares of any size can you find in a 3-by-3 grid of small squares?
cases.notes: 9 of size 1, 4 of size 2, 1 of size 3: 14.

cases.prompt: A 10-metre rope is cut into pieces that are each 2 metres long. Each cut goes through the rope once. How many cuts are needed?
How many days after 1 January 2024 is 1 January 2025?
cases.notes: 2024 is a leap year: 366 days (datetime check in build.py).

cases.prompt: You save 1 cent on day 1, 2 cents on day 2, 3 cents on day 3, and so on, one cent more each day. How many dollars have you saved after 100 days?
cases.notes: 1 + 2 + ... + 100 = 5,050 cents = $50.50. Forgetting to convert gives the lure 5,050.

cases.prompt: How many minutes are there in 1.25 hours?
cases.notes: 0.25 h = 15 min; 60 + 15 = 75. Reading 1.25 h as 1 h 25 min gives 85; decimal-to-minutes slips give 125.

cases.prompt: A student's test score goes up from 40% to 50%. By what percentage of the original score did it increase?
cases.notes: (50 - 40) / 40 = 25%. The 10 percentage points are the lure.

cases.prompt: In a year that is not a leap year, 1 March is a Tuesday. What day of the week is 1 April of the same year?
cases.notes: March has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days, so 1 April is 3 weekdays later: Friday (checked with 2022, where 1 March was a Tuesday).

cases.prompt: Which is largest: 1/3, 0.33 or 33%? Answer with one of the three exactly as written.
